valuation_philosophy.model: Group-level distributable-earnings (FCFE) DCF at cost of equity, no net-debt bridge, mapped onto the dashboard component engine.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_owner_fcf_dcf: Turners is a used-vehicle retailer (Auto Retail, 70% of revenue, 47% of segment NPBT) fused with a NZ$566m consumer/SME finance book (Oxford Finance) and an insurance underwriter (Autosure). NZ$28.1m of interest expense is cost-of-sale for the finance segment, reported OCF is dominated by loan-book growth (FY2026 OCF -75.0 = +44.6 before a -116.1 receivables build), and one syndicated bank facility funds retail property, inventory AND part of the loan book, so neither an EV/WACC DCF nor a clean sum-of-parts split of the debt is possible without inventing an allocation. The dcf-methods routing puts lenders and insurers on post-interest flows capitalised at cost of equity with no debt deduction; the group is valued that way as a whole.
valuation_philosophy.how_the_component_fields_map: ebitda_margin_path = (NPBT + D&A + SBC) / revenue: a post-interest, pre-D&A EARNINGS margin, not EBITDA. lease_cost_pct = IFRS-16 lease principal (treatment B). cash_tax_rate = 28% NZ statutory. da_pct and capex_pct are the Auto Retail property/branch programme (ex-ROU). wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE: it is the equity capital retained to fund finance-receivables growth (and retail working capital), scaled to the change in revenue so it disappears when growth stops. fcf = distributable earnings to shareholders. net_debt = 0 because every dollar of interest is already inside the flows.

segment_cross_check_fy2026.source: FY2026 annual report note 2 and financial review p.10-11

valuation_philosophy.management_targets: FY28 NPBT target NZ$65m now expected in FY27 (annual report, June 2026); FY31 NPBT target NZ$100m set at the March-2026 investor day. Base case lands FY31 NPBT at NZ$97m (slightly below target), bull NZ$114m, bear NZ$64m (flat on FY26 normalised after a trough).
valuation_philosophy.what_the_price_implies: At NZ$7.50 the market is paying 16.4x FY2026 normalised EPS (50.4c) and 2.15x book. On the base driver path that price requires a ~9% cost of equity (required_return_table: 9% -> NZ$7.32), or the bull path at 11%. The house 11% NZD cost of equity makes the stock ~23% overvalued on the weighted basis.

inputs.share_count_basis: 91,025,265 ordinary shares on issue at 31-Mar-2026 (FY2026 AR note 10.1 / NZX disclosures p.5). Diluted weighted average 90,558,849 vs basic 90,522,523: option dilution is 36k shares, immaterial. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The DRP applied to the July-2026 final dividend will have added roughly 0.5-0.9m shares (FY26 DRP issuance 888,406) which is not yet in a filing; a 1% effect.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately zero. Borrowings NZ$586.3m (bank 430.3 + Turners Marque ABS 2025-1 156.1; 31-Mar-2026) fund finance receivables NZ$566.0m, branch property and inventory; all interest (NZ$28.1m) is already deducted inside the NPBT-based flows, and the flows are discounted at cost of equity, so deducting debt again would double-count. Cash NZ$20.2m and the insurance investment portfolio (~NZ$85m at H1 FY26) back operating and insurance liabilities and their income is inside the flows; nothing is stripped, so nothing is added (matching-asset rule). Lease liabilities NZ$20.1m are excluded because lease principal is charged in the flows (treatment B).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 distributable owner FCF on the model's basis, normalised: NPAT 45.6 (ex NZ$7.47m EC Credit goodwill write-down) + D&A 11.097 - capex 41.7 + PP&E disposals 3.304 - lease principal 6.944 - equity retained for loan-book growth (15% x revenue change 37.267 = 5.59) = 5.77. Small because FY2026 was a peak property/branch capex year (Christchurch x3, Napier, Dunedin site). The base year-1 distributable FCF (NZ$13.7m) is component-built, not this figure carried forward.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF -74.981 minus capex 41.7. Meaningless for a lender: the OCF includes a NZ$116.1m net increase in finance receivables (debt-funded loan-book growth), which is operating funding, not cash burn. Before the receivables build OCF was +44.6m.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report cash flow reconciliation / kpis StockBasedComp FY2026 0.862 (FY2025 0.993); no separate net-share-settlement tax line disclosed (staff options settled by share issue: 150,000 shares FY26). SBC is already expensed inside NPBT; it is added back into adj_ebitda and re-deducted via sbc_pct so it is charged exactly once and stays visible.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped. Interest revenue NZ$72.8m is the finance book's operating revenue and NZ$4.2m of insurance investment income backs insurance liabilities; no cash pile is added in the bridge, so nothing is removed from the flows.
inputs.lease_treatment: B: leases as operating cost. Lease principal (1.54% of revenue) charged via lease_cost_pct; lease interest is already inside NPBT; ROU depreciation is inside da_pct and added back like other D&A; lease liabilities excluded from any bridge.
inputs.capex_note: Gross PP&E and intangibles purchases; 40.8 of 42.0 segment acquisitions were Auto Retail (branch property). Six-year average capex/revenue 6.8%; base path 7.5% tapering to 3.0% by FY36 as the 15-branch programme completes (4 new + 2 replacement branches in development for FY28; FY27 'a year of preparation'). This is the single largest lever in the model: holding capex at 4.5% throughout would add roughly NZ$0.65/share.
inputs.buyback_note: No buybacks. The company ISSUES shares under a DRP (888,406 shares / NZ$6.0m in FY26) and staff schemes; the flat count is a modelling convention consistent with full cash distribution of the modelled FCF.
inputs.dividend_policy: 60-70% of NPAT, quarterly, fully imputed; FY26 33.0cps (+14%), 12-year DPS CAGR 10.5%
inputs.guidance_vintage: FY2026 annual report authorised 25-Jun-2026: FY28 NZ$65m NPBT target expected in FY27; FY31 NZ$100m. No FY27 interim print yet (H1 FY27 due ~Nov-2026).
inputs.cost_of_equity_rationale: 11.0% NZD cost of equity: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5% (Sep-2026, assumed) + 1.1 beta x 5.5% NZ equity risk premium = 10.6%, + 0.4% for a NZ$680m-cap NZX name outside the top tier of liquidity. Cyclicality, credit and used-car sourcing risk are charged ONCE, in the probability-weighted scenarios, not as a WACC premium; the same rate is used in all three scenarios. Cross-check: management's own capital framework targets 15% ROE; GEN.NZ (micro-cap NBDT) carries 16.75%, SOFI 12% USD.
notes: MODEL: distributable-earnings (FCFE) DCF at 11% NZD cost of equity, net_debt = 0, 10-year explicit horizon (capex is still tapering from the branch programme and the finance book is still compounding), Gordon terminal capped at 15x distributable FCF (lower than the 20x house default because both the used-car and consumer-credit cycles are inside the flows). Fresh build, no prior TRA.NZ DCF; no MEMORY.md entry.

ROUTING: SKILL.md rows 'operating company' (Auto Retail) + 'non-bank lender' (Oxford Finance) + 'insurer' (Autosure). The parts cannot be valued separately without allocating a shared syndicated facility, so the group is valued on post-interest earnings at cost of equity, which is the lender/insurer treatment; Auto Retail's property capex and Finance's capital retention are charged explicitly so the operating part is not over-valued by an earnings-only capitalisation.

MTF: the user brief mentions an MTF Finance equity stake. It no longer exists: 'Profit on sale of MTF shares' appears in the FY2022 report (line 1069) and the MTF non-recourse ledger was run down by FY2020. The only equity-accounted investee is the 50% Turners Servicing & Repairs JV (carrying value NZ$3.06m, share of loss NZ$0.22m), immaterial and left inside the flows.

EC CREDIT: NZ$7.474m non-cash goodwill write-down in FY26 is excluded from the base-year margin (normalised NPBT 63.224). The business (NZ$1.8m normalised NPBT) is flagged for divestment; no sale proceeds are assumed.

FY2026 was a soft-first-half / record-second-half year: H2 normalised NPBT 32.8m annualises to ~66m, which is why year-1 NPBT of 66.7m sits just above the NZ$65m target despite the late-March 2026 demand softening from the Iran-US conflict noted in the annual report.
PRICE: NZ$7.50 is the NZX regular close of Fri 11-Sep-2026 (not an after-hours print). 52-week range 6.89-9.21; the stock is ~19% off its high.
SBC-light market: SBC is 0.19% of revenue so the house/street band is narrow (weighted 5.78 vs 5.93); band_position is reported but is not economically meaningful here.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Distributable owner FCF (NPAT + D&A - capex - lease principal) FY21..FY26 = 23.3, 20.3, -7.6, 20.0, 11.4, 0.6 (8.1 normalised): lumpy and passes through negative because branch-property capex is front-loaded, so no CAGR is meaningful. Earnings (normalised NPBT) is the growth anchor for this model.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (FY2021-FY2026 book value 233.6 -> 317.9). Base revenue path averages 7.2% over years 1-5 and 5.6% over 10.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR 6.4% is >30% below revenue CAGR 8.7% and normalised-NPBT CAGR 11.1%: expected for a 60-70% payout company that has also grown its loan book on debt (equity/assets 32.5% -> 29.7% in FY26). EPS CAGR (6.1%) matches equity because the DRP added ~1%/yr to the share count.
historical_growth.notes: FY2021 revenue dipped on COVID and the exit from lease-unit sales, so the 5-year revenue CAGR is flattered by a low base; the 6-year (FY2020-26) revenue CAGR is 5.2%.

scenario_narratives.base: Auto Retail keeps its wholesale-to-retail and lower-price-point mix, opens the FY28 branch cohort and grows mid-single digits with owned-stock margins holding; Oxford Finance grows the book low-double digits on stable 5.7% NIM with arrears at 2.5-3%; Autosure compounds premium mid-single digits with MBI loss ratios near 58%; corporate interest keeps falling after the securitisation term-out. NPBT reaches ~NZ$97m by FY31 (target NZ$100m), then growth fades to 3%. Property capex tapers from 7.5% to 3.0% of revenue by FY36; 15% of each revenue dollar added is retained as loan-book equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: The NZ consumer recovery arrives: used-car prices lift, lease-unit and import volumes recover, the 15-branch programme delivers Christchurch-style +22% local sourcing gains, Oxford Finance keeps taking share with the term-out structure requiring only 1.4% capital, and direct-to-consumer insurance scales. NPBT NZ$114m by FY31 (target beaten a year early, as every prior target has been), mature post-interest margin 19.5%, retention 12% of revenue growth, terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The late-March 2026 demand shock persists into a NZ recession: used-car margins compress, a NZ$566m book grown 27% in one year seasons badly (impairments double), NIM is squeezed as hedges roll, and the branch programme is slowed. NPBT troughs at ~NZ$53m in FY28 and only regains FY26's normalised level by FY31; mature margin 15.5%, retention 20% of revenue growth, terminal growth 2%. Note the bear case distributes MORE cash in years 1-2 than base because growth capex and loan-book retention stop: the loss is in the terminal, not the interim flows.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the projected distributable FCF for 10 years and exiting at a terminal value built at the 15% hurdle (min(Gordon@15%, 15x FCF_10)) returns 15% IRR; net_debt = 0. Computed per scenario and probability-weighted.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (cap 15x). 11% row = valuation.base.intrinsic_value; 15% row = entry_price.base.entry_price. The NZ$7.50 price sits between the 9% and 10% rows.

sensitivity.note: Base case, cost of equity x terminal growth. The 15x cap binds across the 9% row (and at 10%/3.5-4%), which is why those cells are flat.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 20% bear / 50% base / 30% bull. Bear lifted from the 15% default because a consumer-credit book that grew 27% in a single year into a two-speed economy (and a demand shock flagged at balance date) is the classic late-cycle set-up, and Auto Retail margins are cyclical; bull trimmed from 35% because it needs the FY31 target to be beaten AND the recovery in used-car pricing to arrive together. Management's record of hitting every target early keeps base at 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is 0.19% of revenue; house and street differ by NZ$0.15/share, so band_position (price relative to the tiny band) is not informative. The price sits far above both.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.checks_replaced: model is earnings_at_coe: P/E and EV/EBITDA trip rules do not apply; the historical table is reported for context only
